title: [Dynamo] Port CPython 3.13 test_copy to Dynamo test suite
body:
## Issue

Part of #196238

## Summary

Ports `test_copy` (the `copy` module: shallow and deep copying of builtins, containers, user classes, slots and weakrefs, the `__reduce__` / `__copy__` / `__deepcopy__` protocols, and `copy.replace`) from CPython v3.13.5 to `test/cpython/v3_13/`, following the standard porting recipe: Dynamo patch header, rebind the three test classes to `CPythonTestCase`, and `run_tests()` footer.

**Result:** 81 tests, 37 pass, 44 recorded as expected failures, no upstream skips. `MiscTestCase` passes in full, `TestReplace` has one failure, and the remaining 43 are in `TestCopy`. The eager control run passes all 81, so nothing here comes from the adaptation itself.

The 44 are **not all the same kind of failure**, and the split is the most useful thing this PR reports:

| kind | n | meaning |
|---|---:|---|
| graph break | 36 | Dynamo cannot trace the construct and says so |
| **wrong answer** | **6** | Dynamo traces it, completes, and returns a **different result than eager** |
| internal crash | 2 | Dynamo's own tracer overflows its Python stack |

## Graph breaks (36)

| gb | n | what |
|---|---:|---|
| `gb0091` | 15 | *"Attempted to read a cell variable that has not been populated yet"* |
| `gb0007` | 5 | untraceable C builtins — `dict.copy`, `list.copy`, `set.copy`, `gc.collect` ×2 |
| `gb0059` | 4 | builtin operators — `bytes`, `bytearray`, `property`, `is_not` |
| `gb0156` | 4 | `tuple.__getnewargs__` ×2, `type.__new__` (via `weakref.ref`) ×2 |
| `gb0008` | 4 | reported as `Unsupported.__init__`; the real construct is `int.__new__(cls)` |
| `gb0147` | 3 | locally defined classes ×2, `<class 'method'>` |
| `gb0467` | 1 | `setattr()` on `type` — `TestReplace.test_dataclass` |

The `gb0091` group: all 15 define a class **inside the test body** whose methods close over a name of the enclosing function that isn't bound yet at class-creation time, and all 15 break at the `class C…:` line. CPython only *stores* the cell at `MAKE_FUNCTION` and never reads it; Dynamo materialises every closure cell eagerly.

## Wrong answers (6)

These do not report an unsupported construct. Dynamo runs the code to completion and produces a different result than eager; the test's own assertion catches it, and only then does it surface as `gb0088` with an underlying `ObservedAssertionError` / `ObservedAttributeError`. All six point at `torch/_dynamo/polyfills/copy.py`:

**1. `listitems` / `dictitems` hardcoded to `None`** — `copy_list_subclass`, `deepcopy_list_subclass`, `deepcopy_dict_subclass`

```python
return (func, newargs, state, None, None)     # polyfills/copy.py
```

CPython's `reduce_newobj` supplies `iter(obj)` for list subclasses and `iter(obj.items())` for dict subclasses, so copying one currently yields an **empty container**. The log records `AssertionError("{'foo': 0} != {}")`.

**2. Slot state dropped** — `copy_slots`, `deepcopy_slots`

`obj.__getstate__()` is called only when the class *overrides* it; otherwise the polyfill falls back to `obj.__dict__`, which raises for a `__slots__`-only class, leaving `state = None`. Consistent with this: `test_copy_inst_getstate` / `test_deepcopy_inst_getstate`, which *do* override `__getstate__`, both pass.

**3. A user-defined `__reduce__` appears not to be consulted** — `reconstruct_string`

`copy.copy(x)` builds a fresh object where it should return `x` itself.

Plain containers are unaffected — `test_deepcopy_list` and `test_deepcopy_dict` pass with the same assertion style — so this is specific to the subclass/slots/`__reduce__` paths.

## Internal crashes (2)

`deepcopy_reflexive_list` and `deepcopy_reflexive_dict` build self-referential containers and assert that comparing them raises `RecursionError`. Dynamo's tracer overflows its own Python stack first (repeated `variables/lists.py` comparison frames), so the error escapes as `InternalTorchDynamoError` and the traced `assertRaises` never observes it.

## Verification

- Anchor pristine hash: **`3dec64cc9a24141d606fe9a0c0e1b9b7f63ed807`** — matches the CPython repo blob for `Lib/test/test_copy.py` at `v3.13.5`.
- `python tools/regenerate_cpython_diffs.py --check` — `OK: 76 cpython .py/.diff pairs in sync` (was 75).
- `PYTORCH_TEST_WITH_DYNAMO=1 python test/cpython/v3_13/test_copy.py -v` — `OK (skipped=44)`, 37 pass.
- `python test/cpython/v3_13/test_copy.py -v` (eager control) — `OK`, all 81 pass, no skips.
- `lintrunner -a` — no lint issues.
- Re-verified after rebasing onto current `main` and upgrading to `torch 2.15.0.dev20260909`: marker set unchanged, no unexpected successes.

## Checklist

- [x] Passes the offline `.py`/`.diff` sync check (76 pairs OK).
- [x] Added expected-failure markers for every non-passing test (44 markers, one per failure).
- [ ] Updated documentation (N/A — test port).
- [ ] Included benchmark results (N/A — no perf impact).

## BC-breaking?

No.

## AI disclosure

Per `AI_POLICY.md`: I fetched the pristine CPython file and applied the porting recipe by hand — prepending the Dynamo patch header, rebinding the three class bases from `unittest.TestCase` to `CPythonTestCase`, and replacing `unittest.main()` with `run_tests()`. The adapted file contains no AI-written code. I generated the anchor `.diff` with the repo's own `tools/regenerate_cpython_diffs.py`, and ran the test, sync-check and lint commands myself. I used an AI assistant to create the empty expected-failure marker files, to cluster the run output by failure cause, and to audit that clustering independently against the Dynamo source — the wrong-answer finding above came out of that audit. Before submitting I read the full diff and checked the marker set against the run output; the marker count matches the failure count exactly, one file per failing test.
